# Introduction

GeneFunnel turns a non-negative feature-by-sample matrix into a
gene-set-by-sample score matrix. It preserves observed magnitude while
penalizing absolute variation among the available members of each set. Every
gene set and sample is calculated independently.

Transcriptomic and proteomic assays commonly use Bioconductor's matrix,
sparse-matrix, and parallel infrastructure. GeneFunnel fits that environment by
accepting base and `Matrix` matrices and a `BiocParallelParam`, while returning
a plain numeric matrix for downstream analysis. It is a scorer only: it does
not normalize data, impute missing values, map identifiers, retrieve gene sets,
or perform statistical testing.

Within a larger pipeline, GeneFunnel can follow assay-specific preprocessing,
identifier mapping, and coverage checks. Its output can then provide
gene-set-level features for sample prioritization, visualization, clustering, or
statistical models.

The package is in development and has not been accepted into Bioconductor. Its
source and issue tracker are on the
[GeneFunnel repository](https://github.com/eturkes/genefunnel).

# Installation

After acceptance, install GeneFunnel from a Bioconductor package repository:

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("genefunnel")
```

During review, replace the package name with `"eturkes/genefunnel"` to install
the development repository.

Load the installed package and choose a serial backend for the first examples.

```{r load}
library(genefunnel)
serial <- BiocParallel::SerialParam()
```

# How the score is calculated

For one declared gene set, GeneFunnel first deduplicates member identifiers and
matches them exactly and case-sensitively to matrix row names. Within sample
$j$, it omits matched values that are `NA` or `NaN`. If the remaining observed
values are $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ and $n \ge 2$, the score is

$$
\bar{x}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i
$$

and

$$
\operatorname{GeneFunnel}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)
=\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i
-\frac{n}{2(n-1)}\sum_{i=1}^{n}|x_i-\bar{x}|.
$$

The cell is `NA_real_` when fewer than two observed members remain. Zero is an
observed value, including an implicit sparse zero, so it participates in $n$,
the sum, the mean, and the deviation. Infinities and negative values are
invalid.

These small examples show the main edge cases.

```{r canonical}
canonical <- matrix(
    c(4, 4, 4, 0, 0, 0, 4, 0, 0, 1, 2, NA, 4, NA, NA),
    nrow = 3,
    dimnames = list(
        c("A", "B", "C"),
        c("equal", "zeros", "one_nonzero", "missing_pair", "one_observed")
    )
)
canonical_sets <- list(
    three_members = c("A", "B", "C"),
    two_members = c("A", "B")
)

canonical_scores <- genefunnel(
    canonical,
    canonical_sets,
    BPPARAM = serial
)
knitr::kable(
    canonical_scores,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c("Equal", "Zeros", "One non-zero", "Missing pair", "One observed")
)

stopifnot(
    identical(
        unname(canonical_scores["three_members", ]),
        c(12, 0, 0, 2, NA_real_)
    ),
    identical(
        unname(canonical_scores["two_members", ]),
        c(8, 0, 0, 2, NA_real_)
    )
)
```

Equal values score their sum. All-zero sets and sets with only one non-zero
member score zero. The missing-pair column scores the observed values `c(1, 2)`
as 2; the last column has only one observed value and returns `NA`.

# Why the penalty matters

A plain member sum cannot distinguish the same total distributed across every
member from a total concentrated in one or two members. The following three
samples all sum to 12.

```{r same-total}
same_total <- rbind(
    A = c(coherent = 3, split = 6, concentrated = 12),
    B = c(coherent = 3, split = 6, concentrated = 0),
    C = c(coherent = 3, split = 0, concentrated = 0),
    D = c(coherent = 3, split = 0, concentrated = 0)
)
same_total_scores <- genefunnel(
    same_total,
    list(pathway = rownames(same_total)),
    BPPARAM = serial
)
same_total_comparison <- data.frame(
    pattern = colnames(same_total),
    observed_sum = unname(colSums(same_total)),
    genefunnel_score = unname(same_total_scores["pathway", ]),
    check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
    same_total_comparison,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c("Pattern", "Observed sum", "GeneFunnel score")
)

stopifnot(
    identical(same_total_comparison$observed_sum, c(12, 12, 12)),
    identical(same_total_comparison$genefunnel_score, c(12, 4, 0))
)
```

GeneFunnel gives full credit to the coherent sample, partial credit to the
two-member split, and zero to the single-feature concentration. This is the
information added by the absolute-deviation penalty. The score is most useful
when agreement within the set is part of the biological question. The example
explains the mathematical difference; it does not show that one method is best
for every analysis.

# Real-data example: presynaptic expression across Braak stages

The [GSE125583](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE125583)
series was released in 2019 and accompanies
[Srinivasan et al. (2020)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2020.107843). It
contains processed bulk RNA-seq from fusiform gyrus tissue of 70 neurologically
normal controls and 219 autopsy-confirmed Alzheimer's disease subjects. GEO
records diagnosis, age, sex, and Braak stage; 287 of the 289 subjects have a
reported stage.

The per-sample processed tables contain size-factor-adjusted RPKM (`nRPKM`) and
raw counts. This vignette embeds the nRPKM values for all subjects and six genes:
`SYN1`, `SYN2`, `SYP`, `SNAP25`, `STX1A`, and `VAMP2`. The source repository's
`data-raw/build-gse125583-example.R` script regenerates the 43 kB fixture from
checksum-verified GEO archives.

The synapsins and synaptophysin represent synaptic-vesicle organization, while
`SNAP25`, `STX1A`, and `VAMP2` form core presynaptic fusion machinery. Together
they provide a compact, fixed presynaptic-release panel. It is an illustrative
panel, not a validated Alzheimer's disease signature or a complete pathway.
Each gene is divided by its median nRPKM among the 70 controls before scoring.
This places the six positive trajectories on a common, non-negative relative
scale; GeneFunnel does not perform that preprocessing itself.

```{r gse125583-pipeline}
gse125583_path <- system.file(
    "extdata",
    "GSE125583_presynaptic_release.csv",
    package = "genefunnel"
)
stopifnot(nzchar(gse125583_path))
gse125583 <- utils::read.csv(
    gse125583_path,
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

presynaptic_genes <- c("SYN1", "SYN2", "SYP", "SNAP25", "STX1A", "VAMP2")
presynaptic_gene_ids <- c(
    SYN1 = 6853L,
    SYN2 = 6854L,
    SYP = 6855L,
    SNAP25 = 6616L,
    STX1A = 6804L,
    VAMP2 = 6844L
)
gse125583_expression <- t(as.matrix(gse125583[presynaptic_genes]))
colnames(gse125583_expression) <- gse125583$sample
storage.mode(gse125583_expression) <- "double"

control_columns <- gse125583$diagnosis == "control"
control_medians <- apply(
    gse125583_expression[, control_columns, drop = FALSE],
    1L,
    median
)
gse125583_relative <- sweep(
    gse125583_expression,
    1L,
    control_medians,
    "/"
)
gse125583_scores <- genefunnel(
    gse125583_relative,
    list(presynaptic_release = presynaptic_genes),
    BPPARAM = serial
)
presynaptic_total <- unname(colSums(gse125583_relative))
presynaptic_score <- unname(gse125583_scores["presynaptic_release", ])
braak_available <- !is.na(gse125583$braak)

gene_summary <- data.frame(
    gene = presynaptic_genes,
    entrez_gene_id = unname(presynaptic_gene_ids[presynaptic_genes]),
    control_median_nrpkm = unname(control_medians[presynaptic_genes]),
    check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
    gene_summary,
    digits = 1,
    col.names = c("Gene", "NCBI Gene ID", "Control median nRPKM")
)

association_summary <- data.frame(
    measure = c("Pearson correlation", "Spearman correlation"),
    six_gene_total = c(
        cor(presynaptic_total[braak_available], gse125583$braak[braak_available]),
        cor(
            presynaptic_total[braak_available],
            gse125583$braak[braak_available],
            method = "spearman"
        )
    ),
    genefunnel_score = c(
        cor(presynaptic_score[braak_available], gse125583$braak[braak_available]),
        cor(
            presynaptic_score[braak_available],
            gse125583$braak[braak_available],
            method = "spearman"
        )
    ),
    check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
    association_summary,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
        "Association with Braak stage",
        "Six-gene total",
        "GeneFunnel score"
    )
)
```

```{r gse125583-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=4.4, fig.cap="Presynaptic expression across Braak stages in GSE125583 fusiform gyrus. A, median control-scaled nRPKM for each selected gene at stages I-VI. B, individual six-gene GeneFunnel scores; black diamonds and lines show stage medians. The display is descriptive and does not fit a disease model."}
braak_stages <- 1:6
braak_labels <- c("I", "II", "III", "IV", "V", "VI")
gene_colours <- c(
    "#4477AA", "#66CCEE", "#228833", "#CCBB44", "#EE6677", "#AA3377"
)
gene_symbols <- c(16, 17, 15, 18, 8, 3)
diagnosis_colours <- c(control = "#4477AA", "Alzheimer's disease" = "#CC6677")
diagnosis_symbols <- c(control = 16, "Alzheimer's disease" = 17)

stage_gene_medians <- vapply(
    braak_stages,
    function(stage) {
        stage_columns <- which(gse125583$braak == stage)
        apply(
            gse125583_relative[, stage_columns, drop = FALSE],
            1L,
            median
        )
    },
    numeric(length(presynaptic_genes))
)
stage_score_medians <- vapply(
    braak_stages,
    function(stage) {
        median(presynaptic_score[which(gse125583$braak == stage)])
    },
    numeric(1L)
)

old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
layout(matrix(c(1, 2), nrow = 1), widths = c(1.15, 1))

par(
    mar = c(4.7, 4.2, 2.2, 0.8),
    mgp = c(2.5, 0.7, 0),
    las = 1,
    bty = "l"
)
matplot(
    braak_stages,
    t(stage_gene_medians),
    type = "o",
    pch = gene_symbols,
    lty = 1,
    lwd = 1.3,
    col = gene_colours,
    xaxt = "n",
    xlab = "Braak stage",
    ylab = "Median expression / control median",
    ylim = range(c(1, stage_gene_medians))
)
axis(1, at = braak_stages, labels = braak_labels)
abline(h = 1, col = "#B3B3B3", lty = 3)
legend(
    "topright",
    legend = presynaptic_genes,
    col = gene_colours,
    pch = gene_symbols,
    lty = 1,
    bty = "n",
    cex = 0.72,
    ncol = 2
)
mtext("A  Selected-gene medians", side = 3, adj = 0, font = 2)

par(
    mar = c(4.7, 4.2, 2.2, 0.8),
    mgp = c(2.5, 0.7, 0),
    las = 1,
    bty = "l"
)
plot(
    NA,
    xlim = c(0.65, 6.35),
    ylim = c(0, max(presynaptic_score) * 1.04),
    xaxt = "n",
    xlab = "Braak stage",
    ylab = "GeneFunnel score"
)
axis(1, at = braak_stages, labels = braak_labels)
for (stage in braak_stages) {
    sample_indices <- which(gse125583$braak == stage)
    offsets <- seq(-0.18, 0.18, length.out = length(sample_indices))
    sample_diagnoses <- gse125583$diagnosis[sample_indices]
    points(
        stage + offsets,
        presynaptic_score[sample_indices],
        pch = unname(diagnosis_symbols[sample_diagnoses]),
        col = grDevices::adjustcolor(
            unname(diagnosis_colours[sample_diagnoses]),
            alpha.f = 0.55
        ),
        cex = 0.72
    )
}
lines(braak_stages, stage_score_medians, col = "#222222", lwd = 1.5)
points(
    braak_stages,
    stage_score_medians,
    pch = 18,
    col = "#222222",
    cex = 1.05
)
legend(
    "topright",
    legend = c("Control", "Alzheimer's disease", "Stage median"),
    col = c(unname(diagnosis_colours), "#222222"),
    pch = c(unname(diagnosis_symbols), 18),
    bty = "n",
    cex = 0.72
)
mtext("B  Panel score", side = 3, adj = 0, font = 2)

layout(1)
par(old_par)
```

```{r gse125583-pipeline-check, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(
    identical(dim(gse125583_expression), c(6L, 289L)),
    identical(
        as.integer(table(gse125583$diagnosis)[
            c("Alzheimer's disease", "control")
        ]),
        c(219L, 70L)
    ),
    sum(braak_available) == 287L,
    all(gse125583_expression > 0),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        control_medians,
        c(
            SYN1 = 119.521414801991,
            SYN2 = 53.495229040887,
            SYP = 230.823767700279,
            SNAP25 = 547.602073827910,
            STX1A = 68.824085690708,
            VAMP2 = 231.024436070715
        ),
        tolerance = 1e-10
    )),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        apply(
            gse125583_relative[, control_columns, drop = FALSE],
            1L,
            median
        ),
        stats::setNames(rep(1, 6), presynaptic_genes),
        tolerance = 1e-12
    )),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        presynaptic_score[c(1, 13, 101, 289)],
        c(3.11895741616489, 5.76116235839454, 5.17394506339094,
            7.02428095444394),
        tolerance = 1e-10
    )),
    isTRUE(all.equal(
        cor(
            presynaptic_score[braak_available],
            gse125583$braak[braak_available],
            method = "spearman"
        ),
        -0.4092210329,
        tolerance = 1e-10
    ))
)
```

Across the 287 subjects with a recorded stage, the GeneFunnel score has a
Spearman correlation of -0.409 with Braak stage; the plain six-gene total has a
correlation of -0.393. The stage-median score decreases from 6.39 at stage I to
1.93 at stage VI, although adjacent stages are not strictly monotonic.
GeneFunnel's contribution is the sample-specific disagreement penalty, not a
claim that this compact panel has a materially stronger pathology association
than its sum.

The result is descriptive. Braak stage and diagnosis are closely related in
this autopsy cohort, and the calculation does not adjust for age, sex, technical
variation, or tissue cell composition. It also does not fit or test an
association. A full analysis should predeclare a complete gene set and
preprocessing plan, assess coverage, and use an appropriate downstream model.
The six-gene panel is an inspectable scoring example, not a biomarker.

# Choosing between GeneFunnel and rank-based methods

Gene-set scoring is already supported by several complementary packages.
[`GSVA`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/GSVA) offers unsupervised gene-set
transformations whose methods use relative expression or rank information.
[`singscore`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/singscore) and
[`UCell`](https://bioconductor.org/packages/UCell) calculate single-sample
scores from within-sample feature ranks, with UCell using a Mann-Whitney U
statistic.

GeneFunnel answers a different question. It does not rank values or estimate a
distribution across samples. Instead, it applies the formula above to each set
and sample independently. The score therefore depends on measurement scale,
set size, and observed coverage. Choose the method that matches the quantity
you want to preserve.

# Check coverage before scoring

A declared member absent from the matrix changes global assay coverage. It is
different from a missing cell, which affects only one sample, and from an
observed zero. `gene_set_coverage()` exposes these facts before scoring.

```{r coverage}
catalogue <- list(
    complete = c("A", "B"),
    partial = c("A", "B", "D"),
    duplicated = c("A", "A", "B"),
    insufficient = c("A", "Z")
)
coverage <- gene_set_coverage(catalogue, rownames(canonical))
knitr::kable(
    coverage,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c(
        "Gene set",
        "Declared",
        "Matched",
        "Unmatched",
        "Coverage",
        "Duplicates",
        "Scoreable"
    )
)
```

GeneFunnel can score a set whenever at least two unique members match. It does
not impose a coverage fraction because suitable thresholds depend on the
experiment. A transcriptomic analysis might require complete coverage:

```{r strict-coverage}
strict <- !is.na(coverage$coverage) & coverage$coverage == 1
names(catalogue[strict])
```

A low-coverage proteomic analysis might require at least 50% coverage and at
least two matched members:

```{r relaxed-coverage}
relaxed <- !is.na(coverage$coverage) &
    coverage$coverage >= 0.5 &
    coverage$matched_size >= 2
names(catalogue[relaxed])

relaxed_scores <- genefunnel(
    canonical,
    catalogue[relaxed],
    BPPARAM = serial
)
knitr::kable(
    relaxed_scores,
    digits = 3,
    col.names = c("Equal", "Zeros", "One non-zero", "Missing pair", "One observed")
)
```

These thresholds are examples rather than package recommendations. Record the
gene-set collection, its version, and the threshold used in the analysis.

# Dense and sparse matrices

Sparse input stays sparse through scoring, and implicit zeros remain observed.
Stored sparse `NA` and `NaN` values follow the same sample-specific omission
rule as dense missing values.

```{r sparse}
sparse_canonical <- Matrix::Matrix(canonical, sparse = TRUE)
sparse_scores <- genefunnel(
    sparse_canonical,
    canonical_sets,
    BPPARAM = serial
)

isTRUE(all.equal(
    sparse_scores,
    canonical_scores,
    tolerance = 0,
    check.attributes = TRUE
))
```

The dense and sparse implementations are required to produce the same named
matrix. Sparse storage changes memory use and traversal, not the scientific
calculation.

# Serial and parallel execution

`BPPARAM` accepts any suitable `BiocParallelParam`. `SerialParam()` is useful
for debugging and small inputs. A portable SOCK backend can distribute bounded
column chunks while preserving sample order.

```{r parallel}
sock <- BiocParallel::bpstart(BiocParallel::SnowParam(
    workers = 2L,
    type = "SOCK",
    progressbar = FALSE
))
parallel_scores <- tryCatch(
    genefunnel(canonical, canonical_sets, BPPARAM = sock),
    finally = BiocParallel::bpstop(sock)
)

identical(parallel_scores, canonical_scores)
```

Process startup and data transfer can outweigh parallel work on small inputs.
Benchmark the intended workload rather than assuming that more workers are
faster.

# Identifiers and preprocessing

Matrix row names and gene-set names must be unique, non-missing, and non-empty.
Member matching is exact, with no case conversion, synonym resolution, or
annotation lookup. Duplicated members within one set are counted in coverage
diagnostics and deduplicated for scoring. Overlapping sets remain valid and do
not influence one another.

GeneFunnel requires non-negative input with a meaningful zero. It applies no
automatic preprocessing. An arbitrary positive shift is unsuitable because
adding a constant $c$ to all $n$ observed members adds $nc$ to the score. Raw
non-negative measurements can be preferable when scientifically appropriate,
but the package does not prescribe a universal pipeline position.

# Interpretation and limitations

The absolute-deviation penalty treats within-set variability as evidence
against coherent activity. That is a scientific assumption rather than a
universal property of biological pathways.

The sum term preserves magnitude and therefore also preserves effects of input
units, library size, preprocessing, set size, and feature coverage. Independent
sample scoring does not make scores from unrelated data sets automatically
comparable. Such comparisons require compatible units, preprocessing,
identifiers, gene-set definitions, versions, and coverage policies.

Gene-set database revisions can change scores. The package does not guarantee
that the resulting distribution meets the assumptions of every downstream
statistical method. Validate those assumptions for the intended analysis.

The full scoring specification is installed as `SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md`:

```{r specification-path}
specification <- system.file("SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md", package = "genefunnel")
stopifnot(nzchar(specification), file.exists(specification))
basename(specification)
```
